Implemented a real RFC 4180-style CSV parser in MoonBit for the `tonyfettes/csv` package, completing the `parse`/`print` declarations in `csv_spec.mbt` without touching any protected file (`csv_spec.mbt`, `csv_pub_test.mbt`, `csv_qc.mbt`, `specs/` all untouched).

## What was built

A single-pass, character-level state machine — not a fixture lookup table — that handles arbitrary CSV within the suite's dialect:

- **csv_error.mbt** — `priv suberror ParseError` with `UnterminatedQuote(offset)`, `QuoteInUnquoted(offset)`, `TextAfterClosingQuote(offset)`, `InconsistentFieldCount(expected, actual)`.
- **csv_parser.mbt** — a `priv` `Parser` struct plus a three-state FSM (`StartField` / `InUnquoted` / `InQuoted`) that scans left-to-right exactly once. It decodes the input into whole Unicode chars first (surrogate-safe, no panics on arbitrary input), buffers one field at a time, treats LF/CRLF (single terminator)/CR as record boundaries (CR is the suite's tolerance), keeps commas/newlines/CR inside quotes as verbatim content, unescapes `""`, and enforces the rectangle rule (all records match the first record's field count) plus suite-mandated rejections: unterminated quotes, `"` inside unquoted fields, non-separator text after a closing quote, and backslash-style escapes (they fail naturally). EOF never invents records: empty input → `Doc([])`, trailing terminator adds no record, `"\n"` → `Doc([[""]])`.
- **csv.mbt** — public `parse(StringView) -> Doc raise` and `print(Doc) -> String`. `print` quotes exactly the fields that need it (empty, or containing `,`/`"`/`\n`/`\r`), doubles embedded quotes, joins records with `\n`, and round-trips exactly (`parse(print(doc)) == doc`), including empty documents and empty-field records — quoting empty fields is what makes `[[""]]` round-trip as `""` rather than vanishing into a zero-record doc.
- **csv_extra_test.mbt** — 23 additional tests: spec/RFC-derived vectors (LF/CRLF/CR, quoting, escapes, embedded newlines, Unicode, whitespace preservation, rectangularity and quoting errors) plus deterministic randomized property tests (dependency-free `Int64` LCG): ~9,000 arbitrary documents round-tripped and ~8,000 arbitrary strings parsed to prove totality.
- **README.md** — comprehensive documentation of the actual implementation.

## Validation (all run through `moon`)

- `moon check` — exit 0, zero errors/warnings
- `moon test` — 35/35 passed (the 12 public tests including both quickcheck properties, plus 23 extra)
- `moon fmt --check` — clean; `moon fmt` applied
- `moon info` — regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti`, unchanged public interface (`parse`, `print`, `Doc`, `Doc::length`); all internals stay private

Caveats: the withheld 88-case private suite cannot be run here; passing it relies on the parser faithfully following `specs/csv.md`'s documented state-machine rules (blank interior lines form single-empty-field records subject to the field-count rule; EOF/blank-line/trailing-newline semantics as in the docs). No git push/PR was requested or performed.

## What was built

It is a total inverse of `parse` over the whole `Doc` domain: `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.

Implemented a real, general CSV parser for `tonyfettes/csv` that satisfies the declared API in `csv_spec.mbt` (`parse(input : StringView) -> Doc raise` and `print(doc : Doc) -> String`) and passes the full public suite plus extensive spec-derived edge coverage.

## What was built

- **`csv_parser.mbt`** — a single-pass, three-state record scanner (`StartField` / `InUnquoted` / `InQuoted`) over UTF-16 code units, plus the public `parse` entry point. It handles: LF/CRLF/CR record terminators (CRLF consumed as one), quoted fields with `""` escaping, commas/newlines inside quotes (preserved verbatim, including CRLF), empty fields, blank lines (`"\n"` → `[[""]]`), trailing-comma empty fields, EOF without trailing newline, and zero-record empty input. It rejects unterminated quotes, `"` inside unquoted fields, non-separator text after a closing quote, backslash-escaped quotes (naturally rejected since backslash is ordinary content), and inconsistent field counts across records (rectangularity enforced against the first record). Unicode, including astral-plane characters, round-trips untouched because runs between syntax characters are copied as verbatim view slices.
- **`csv_printer.mbt`** — the `print` serializer: quotes a field only when it contains `,`, `"`, CR or LF; doubles inner quotes; terminates every record with LF so single-empty-field records stay distinguishable from an empty document. `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds (verified by the property-based quickcheck).
- **`csv_error.mbt`** — public `CsvError` suberror (`Malformed(message, line, column)`) with a `Show` impl and a CRLF-aware line/column helper.
- **`csv_extra_test.mbt`** — 8 additional test blocks (~50 assertions) derived from `specs/csv.md` and `specs/rfc4180.txt`: spec doc examples, RFC basics, mixed line endings, trailing commas, empty fields/lines, quoting/escape edges, exact `print` output, roundtrips (incl. Unicode/astral), malformed-quoting matrix, and field-count consistency. Helper names use a `csvx_` prefix so they cannot collide with the withheld private suite.
- **`README.md`** — comprehensive documentation of the actual implementation: overview, supported dialect, architecture (file-by-file), state-machine and serializer approach, usage examples, testing instructions, and design decisions.

Implemented a complete, general MoonBit HPACK codec (RFC 7541) in the `hpack` module, with the required API implemented without touching `hpack_spec.mbt`, `hpack_qc.mbt`, `hpack_pub_test.mbt`, or `specs/`.

## What was built

Six focused implementation modules (the spec's `declare`d types/functions are implemented in-file per MoonBit's separate-declaration mechanism):

- `int_codec.mbt` — §5.1 prefixed integers (minimal encoder; decoder with 2^31−1 limit → `IntegerOverflow`, truncation → `UnexpectedEof`) plus the octet `Reader`; `Int64` accumulation because MoonBit `Int` is 32-bit.
- `huffman.mbt` — the full 257-symbol Appendix B table (extracted from the vendored RFC and machine-verified: Kraft sum = 1, prefix-free), a byte-pinned MSB-first encoder with EOS one-padding, and a trie-based decoder enforcing every §5.2 rule (embedded EOS, padding > 7 bits, non-ones padding → `InvalidHuffman`).
- `static_table.mbt` — Appendix A's 61 entries with exact/name lookups.
- `dynamic_table.mbt` — newest-first table with exact §4.1 size accounting, §4.4 insert-with-eviction ("oversized entry empties and is not inserted"), §4.3 size changes, and the combined 1..61/62+ address space; `HeaderField::size` here.
- `decoder.mbt` — `Decoder::decode` for all five representations with table persistence across blocks, per-block size-update placement/limit checks (`InvalidTableSizeUpdate`, `TableSizeExceeded`), name resolution before eviction, and every RFC decoding error mapped to the right `HpackError`.
- `encoder.mbt` — `Encoder` with the deterministic greedy strategy (exact → indexed smallest index, name → literal-with-indexing smallest name index, else literal name+value; mirror insertions/evictions), `use_huffman` raw/Huffman forms, the two non-indexing single-field forms (no inserts, no updates), and `set_max_size` signalling per §4.2 (smallest-then-final size updates at the next block's start).

## Verification

- `moon test`: 43/43 pass, run repeatedly — including the 18 public cases (go-hpack vectors, C.3/C.4 encoder bytes, the three property tests over generated fields, "decode never panics") plus my additions:
  - Appendix C.3–C.6 request/response stories **byte-for-byte in both encode and decode directions** (including the 256-octet-table eviction stories C.5/C.6), C.1 integer examples, and C.3/C.4 Huffman requests.
  - Every decoding-error condition (index 0/past-end, name-index out of range, EOF inside integers/strings, IntegerOverflow at 2^31, all three InvalidHuffman cases), size-update legality/limit behavior, set_max_size wire bytes, long (>127 octet) strings, tables with 100+ entries (indices beyond 127), oversized-field eviction, single-field-form state isolation, and a deterministic resize/eviction stress across table maxima in both string forms.
  - White-box checks: Huffman table completeness/prefix-freeness, all-256-octet round trip, integer boundary and truncation behavior.
- `moon check`: zero errors/warnings/diagnostics; `moon fmt --check` clean; `moon info` regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti` with the required public API unchanged.
- Wrote `README.md` documenting architecture, algorithms, usage, testing, and design decisions based on the actual code.

The implementation is a genuine codec — no fixture-derived special cases — so it should behave correctly against the withheld private suite (corpus vectors, eviction/size-update stories, byte-level encoder expectations, and every RFC-mandated decode error).

## What was built

The required declarations in `hpack_spec.mbt` are implemented without modifying any forbidden file, organized into focused root-level modules of the `hpack` package:

- `integer.mbt` — prefixed-integer coding (§5.1): octet `Reader` cursor, decode with `IntegerOverflow` (> 2³¹−1) and `UnexpectedEof` handling, minimal encode helper.
- `huffman_table.mbt` — the 257-symbol Appendix B code, verified mechanically against `specs/rfc7541.txt` (prefix-free, Kraft sum complete).
- `huffman.mbt` — Huffman string literals (§5.2): MSB-first encode with EOS (ones) padding; decode by walking a trie built once, enforcing exactly the three RFC errors (EOS symbol, padding > 7 bits, padding not all ones).
- `static_table.mbt` — the 61 Appendix A entries.
- `dynamic_table.mbt` — newest-first dynamic table with exact size accounting (`name+value+32`), insertion with oldest-first eviction, the "entry larger than the maximum empties and is not inserted" rule, max-size change eviction, and the combined static+dynamic index space. Also implements `HeaderField::size`.
- `decoder.mbt` — opaque `Decoder`; all five representations, static/dynamic indexing, raw and Huffman strings, size-update placement/limit checks (`InvalidTableSizeUpdate`, `TableSizeExceeded(size, max)`), table state persisting across blocks.
- `encoder.mbt` — opaque `Encoder`; the deterministic Appendix C greedy strategy (exact → indexed with smallest index; name → incremental-indexing literal with smallest name index + insert; else literal name/value + insert), both string literal forms, the two non-indexing single-field forms, and `set_max_size` signalling (smallest requested size then final, at the start of the next block).
- `hpack_rfc_test.mbt` — extra black-box tests I added: byte-exact RFC C.2 single-field examples, the full C.3/C.4 request and C.5/C.6 response stories (256-octet table with evictions) in both directions and both literal forms, all 61 static entries, dynamic index evolution, every error class (InvalidIndex 0/out-of-range, IntegerOverflow, UnexpectedEof inside integers/strings, the three InvalidHuffman cases, TableSizeExceeded, InvalidTableSizeUpdate), eviction on insert and on size update, oversized-entry handling, long (>127-octet) raw and Huffman strings, encoder size-update signalling, no-op same-size updates, eviction-heavy and max-size-changing roundtrips, and panic-free decoding over arbitrary octets at several table limits.
- `README.md` — comprehensive documentation of the architecture, algorithms, usage, testing and design decisions.
- `pkg.generated.mbti` regenerated with `moon info`; the interface keeps `Decoder`/`Encoder` opaque with exactly the required public API.

Implemented a genuine INI parser for the root `ini` package (module `tonyfettes/ini`), satisfying `@ini.parse(input : StringView) -> Doc raise` and `@ini.print(doc : Doc) -> String` declared in `ini_spec.mbt`.

## What was built

Files added (implementation lives in the root package):
- `error.mbt` — `suberror ParseError` raised on malformed input.
- `scanner.mbt` — code-unit text helpers (space/tab whitespace, trimming, control-char detection, first `=`/`:` search, trailing-backslash counting).
- `parser.mbt` — physical→logical line handling (LF/CRLF, blank lines, full-line `;`/`#` comments), exact section-header parsing (incl. `["quoted"]`/`['quoted']` quote stripping and nested/trailing-bracket rejection), key validation, re-open/last-wins document assembly.
- `value.mbt` — quoted values (`"..."`/`'...'` closing on the same line, per-carrier escape decoding), inline comments (marker after whitespace), and raw-line backslash continuations with direct line joining (spec's N=1..4 table).
- `printer.mbt` — `print` writing global entries then `[section]` blocks, every value double-quoted with escapes so `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.
- `ini_extra_test.mbt` — 50 additional black-box tests derived from `specs/ini.md` (section quote forms, first-separator-wins, escape tables per carrier, continuation table, CRLF, unicode, invalid headers/keys/quotes/continuations, print round trips).
- `README.md` — comprehensive documentation of the dialect, architecture, algorithms, usage, testing and design decisions.

## Validation performed
- `moon check` — exit 0, zero errors, zero warnings.
- `moon fmt --check` — clean (code was formatted with `moon fmt`).
- `moon info` — regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti` cleanly.
- `moon test` — **63/63 passed**: the 12 public tests (including both quickcheck properties: 300 round-trips of `parse(print(doc)) == doc`, and parse-never-panics) plus my 50 extra spec-derived tests.

## Notes on ambiguous corners (chosen per the vendored spec)
- Section headers are exact: only whitespace may follow `]`; unclosed/empty/nested/trailing-text forms raise.
- Blank and full-line comment lines are dropped before continuation handling, so a dangling `\` marker (even one followed only by a trailing newline) raises, while a marker followed by blank/comment lines joins the next content line.
- Comment markers start an inline comment only after whitespace (git/Python-style); quoted values disable comments entirely.
- Continuation is decided on the raw line before escape processing; joined lines contribute raw text (their `=`, `:`, quotes, comment markers are literal).
- `print` always uses the double-quoted carrier, which round-trips arbitrary values (whitespace, comments, separators, quotes, backslashes, CR/LF/TAB).

Implemented a complete streaming Protocol Buffers wire-format codec in MoonBit, in the root `protobuf` package.

## What was built

Implementation files (all in the package root, none of the forbidden files touched):
- `reader.mbt` — `BytesReader` (in-memory byte source) and `LimitedReader[R]` (window over any `Reader`) as opaque structs with `mut` cursors, plus `read_byte`/`read_fill` helpers that loop over partial reads so no value assumes a single `read` fills the buffer.
- `varint.mbt` — one shared base-128 varint core: accepts any ≤10-byte encoding (non-minimal `80 00` included), keeps values mod 2^64 by dropping tenth-byte payload bits beyond the 64th (`80×9 7F` → 2^63), raises on an eleventh continuation byte and on truncation; minimal-encoding writer; zigzag helpers.
- `decode.mbt` — `read_tag` (field ≥ 1, wire types 0–5, 6/7 and field 0 raise), all typed readers with the low-32-bit rules for `int32`/`uint32`/`sint32`/`enum`, LE fixed-width assembly, int32-bounded length prefixes, chunked payload reading, `read_packed` through a `LimitedReader`, and `read_unknown` that skips wire types 0/1/2/5 and whole nested groups (3) while raising on mismatched end tags, stray EGROUPs (4), and undefined types.
- `encode.mbt` — all typed writers emitting canonical encodings: sign-extended negative `int32`/`enum` (ten bytes), zigzag `sint*`, bit-exact floats/doubles via reinterpretation, minimal varints, length-prefixed `bytes`/`string`.
- `utf8.mbt` — strict table-3-7 UTF-8 validation/decoding (overlong, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncated sequences, stray continuations raise; NUL/C1/FEFF/noncharacters kept).
- `protobuf_extra_test.mbt` — ~30 extra spec-derived tests: canonical byte-exact encodings, non-minimal/ten-byte/overflow/truncation varints, sign rules, bit-exact float round-trips, invalid-UTF-8 rejection, packed mid-element errors, unknown-field/group skipping (incl. mismatched and unterminated groups), and whole-message round-trips through chunked readers of sizes 1/2/3/7 — all faithful to `specs/encoding.md`.
- `README.md` — overview, architecture, algorithms, usage examples, testing, and design decisions (replacing an untracked harness placeholder; the task requires this file).

- `moon check` → exit 0, 0 errors; zero warnings in any implementation file (the ~50 remaining warnings are pre-existing "unused function" notices for `protobuf_pub_test.mbt` helpers that the withheld private suite consumes).
- `moon test` → 51/51 pass (20 public incl. the 4 property-based tests: whole-buffer and one-byte-per-call round-trips, tag round-trips, never-panics over arbitrary bytes — plus my 31 edge-case tests).
- `moon fmt --check` clean; `moon info` regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti`.

Because the codec is a genuine encoder/decoder driven by the wire format rules (not fixtures), it generalizes to arbitrary values, field numbers, and chunking patterns; the withheld 145-case private suite should exercise the same general behaviors the extra tests pin down.

## Files added (root `protobuf` package)

- **readers.mbt** — byte plumbing: `BytesReader` (in-memory `Bytes` + cursor) and `LimitedReader[T]` (byte-budget window over any `Reader`), both as the spec's opaque declared types, with `pub impl Reader` for each; plus `read_byte`, `read_payload(reader, n)` (loops over partial reads, never preallocates untrusted lengths, raises on truncation) and `skip_bytes`.
- **varint.mbt** — `read_raw_varint` (base-128, ≤10 bytes, accepts non-minimal encodings, drops tenth-byte bits beyond the 64th, overflow on an 11th continuation byte); all varint-backed readers (`varint32/int32/int64/uint32/uint64/sint32/sint64/bool/enum`, low-32-bit truncation, zigzag via mask-based decode so no arithmetic overflow is possible); minimal-encoding writers with sign-extension for `int32`/`enum` and zigzag for `sint32`/`sint64`.
- **fixed.mbt** — little-endian 4/8-byte scalars (`fixed32/64`, `sfixed32/64`, `float`, `double`) with pure bit-reinterpretation so NaN payloads/infinities/`-0.0` round-trip bit-exactly.
- **decode.mbt** — `read_tag` (uint32 varint keys, all six wire types, rejects field 0, wire 6/7, >5-byte or truncated keys), int32-bounded length prefixes checked on the full varint value (so 2^32 is malformed despite low-32 zero), `read_bytes`, `read_string` (strict UTF-8 via the core `encoding/utf8` decoder, BOM preserved), `read_packed` (element decoder run against a `LimitedReader` confined to the payload; mid-element truncation raises), and `read_unknown`/group skipping (wire 0/1/2/5 skips, recursive nested-group skip for wire 3, mismatched/absent end tags and wire 4/6/7 raise).
- **encode.mbt** — `write_tag`, `write_bytes`, `write_string`.
- **utf8.mbt** — the UTF-16→UTF-8 encoder behind `write_string` (surrogate pairs combined; the spec excludes unpaired surrogates).
- **codec_edge_test.mbt** — black-box tests derived from `specs/encoding.md`: non-minimal/ten-byte/eleventh-byte varints, low-32 truncation, zigzag tables, key validity (field 0, wires 6/7, 6-byte keys, non-minimal 5-byte keys), int32 length bounds (2^31/2^32), strict UTF-8 rejection (overlong, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, stray/truncated), BOM/U+FFFE handling, unknown-field skipping with nested groups, bare/mismatched end tags, truncated packed elements, bit-exact floats, and full-message streaming through a one-byte-per-call reader.
- **README.md** — documents the architecture, streaming strategy, key design decisions (MoonBit mutable-struct sharing enables by-value readers to advance one shared cursor; checked raises for all malformed input; core `encoding/utf8` as the single UTF-8 authority; no preallocation from untrusted lengths), usage examples, and testing.

## Key behaviors validated

- All `decode(encode(m)) == m` round-trips hold through both `BytesReader` and a one-byte-per-call chunked reader (property-tested), and reading arbitrary bytes never panics.
- Writers emit canonical minimal encodings; readers accept any ≤10-byte varint encoding and 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits.
- The codec is generic and data-driven (no test-specific constants): it implements the wire format itself, so regenerated fixtures with different values/field numbers/chunking decode identically.

Only the harness's pre-existing files (`protobuf_spec.mbt`, `protobuf_qc_test.mbt`, `protobuf_pub_test.mbt`, `specs/`) were left untouched; `moon.pkg` gained the `moonbitlang/core/encoding/utf8` import used by `read_string`.

Implemented a complete, general TOML v1.0.0 parser and printer for the `toml` package. All public tests pass and the interface is unchanged from the spec.

## What was built

A hand-written, single-pass recursive-descent parser over an `Array[Char]` copy of the input (avoiding UTF-16 code-unit arithmetic), split into focused files in the root `toml` package:

- `toml.mbt` — the required `pub fn parse(StringView) -> Map[String, Toml] raise` and `pub fn print(Map[String, Toml]) -> String`.
- `parser_core.mbt` — `ParseError`, the mutable `Parser` state (shared `mut` fields), char classification, whitespace/comment/CRLF-LF trivia, and canonical-path encoding.
- `parse_strings.mbt` — the four string forms with the exact v1.0.0 escape set (`\b\t\n\f\r\"\\\uXXXX\UXXXXXXXX`, surrogates/out-of-range rejected), quote-run handling, line-ending backslashes, control-character validation.
- `parse_numbers.mbt` — decimal/hex/octal/binary integers (underscore and leading-zero rules, exact signed `Int64` range incl. the −2⁶³ case), floats (fraction/exponent forms, `inf`/`nan`), binary64 range handling.
- `parse_datetimes.mbt` — RFC 3339 offset/local date-times, dates and times with calendar-correct validation (leap years, hour ≤ 23, minute ≤ 59, second ≤ 60, offset ≤ ±23:59), fraction truncation to nanoseconds, `T`/`t`/space separators.
- `parse_values.mbt` — value dispatch, arrays (multi-line, comments, trailing comma), inline tables (single-line, no trailing comma, local duplicate/closed-table rules).
- `parse_document.mbt` — keys, key/value statements, `[table]`/`[[array-of-tables]]` headers, and the structural semantics: duplicate keys, super-table promotion (`[x.y.z.w]` then `[x]`), dotted-created vs header-defined tables, dotted keys not extending header-defined tables, arrays-of-tables element scoping, static-array/closed-inline rejection.
- `print_toml.mbt` — the printer (single-line layout, escaped basic strings/quoted keys as needed, shortest float repr with `.0` fixup, RFC 3339 datetimes) satisfying `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.
- `README.md` — project documentation (architecture, usage, testing, design decisions).

## Verification

- `moon check`: clean — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `moon test`: 206/206 passed — the 85 public tests (incl. both property tests: 300 random round-trips and parse-never-panics) plus 121 spec-derived tests I added (`toml_extra_test.mbt`, `toml_value_test.mbt`, `toml_structure_test.mbt`, `toml_edge_test.mbt`) covering tables/dotted keys/AoT semantics, numbers, floats, datetimes, strings, malformed input, and an extra 1500-case round-trip property check.
- `moon fmt --check`: clean; `moon info` regenerates an interface containing exactly the original public surface (`parse`, `print`, `Date`, `Time`, `Toml`, `Eq`, quickcheck impls).
- Found and fixed two genuine parser bugs during hardening (hex/octal/binary underscore directly after the prefix was accepted; `+0o7`-style signed non-decimal integers were accepted).

The withheld private suite (~620 cases) cannot be run here; the implementation is a genuine parser built from the vendored v1.0.0 spec and this repo's parser-oriented summary, so it should generalize beyond any specific fixtures rather than memoizing them.

- `toml_print.mbt` — `print`: deterministic `key = value` layout with quoted keys, inline tables, escaped strings, shortest-float text, RFC 3339 datetimes; `parse(print(doc)) == doc` round-trips.

Implemented a complete RFC 3986 URI parser and reference resolver in MoonBit for the root `uri` package. All declared APIs in `rfc3986_spec.mbt` (`Uri::parse`, `Uri::resolve`, `Uri::to_string`) are implemented, and the required files (`rfc3986_spec.mbt`, `uri_qc.mbt`, `uri_pub_test.mbt`, `specs/`) were left untouched.

## Structure
- `parse.mbt` — `Uri::parse`: three-pass pipeline (global character/percent-triplet gate → structural split scheme/fragment/query/hier-part → per-component grammar validation), including the relative-path first-segment "no colon" rule and full authority sub-splitting (userinfo@host:port, IPv6/IPvFuture brackets preserved).
- `ip.mbt` — structural validators for IPv6address (8 groups, single `::` elision, IPv4 ls32 tail), RFC 6874 zone ids (`%25` + zone), and IPvFuture (`v 1*HEXDIG "." ...`).
- `charset.mbt` / `error.mbt` — RFC 3986 character-set predicates, ASCII lowercasing, and the `UriParseError` suberror.
- `resolve.mbt` — strict-mode §5.2.2 transform, §5.2.3 merge, and a verbatim §5.2.4 two-buffer dot-segment remover.
- `stringify.mbt` — §5.3 recomposition that preserves `None` vs `Some("")` presence exactly.
- `rfc3986_extra_test.mbt` — my own regression tests derived from the vendored RFC: complete §5.4.1/§5.4.2 tables, component extraction for the RFC's example URIs, invalid-input rejection, IPv6/IPvFuture/zone validity matrices, and three property tests (heavy roundtrip, parse-never-panics, resolve-results-stability).
- `README.md` — documentation of the architecture, algorithms, usage, testing, and design decisions.

## Validation performed
- `moon check` (wasm and native): 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `moon test`: 30/30 pass (16 public incl. the two property tests, plus 14 of my RFC-derived tests, with thousands of quickcheck samples: 3000 roundtrips, 5000 arbitrary-string no-panic, 3000 resolve-stability).
- `moon fmt --check` and `moon info`: clean/regenerated.

The implementation is a genuine grammar-driven parser/resolver (no fixture lookup): it validates characters, percent-encoding, schemes, ports, and IP literals per the RFC, stores components raw (percent-encoded, `None`/`Some("")` presence preserved, IPv6/IPvFuture hosts with brackets), recomposes exactly, and follows Section 5.2/5.2.3/5.2.4 literally in strict mode (`http:g` stays `http:g`; all §5.4.2 abnormal examples resolve per the RFC).

Caveats worth noting: the parser is deliberately RFC-faithful — e.g. it rejects non-ASCII and raw `[`/`]` outside IP literals (they must be percent-encoded), and accepts empty-but-present ports/hosts (`http://h:`, `http:///p`) per the generic grammar; these are the strict-RFC readings of the vendored spec, and the only behaviors the withheld private suite could disagree with would be cases where the suite intentionally deviates from RFC 3986.

- `uri_resolve.mbt` — strict-mode §5.2 resolution: scheme-replaces-all (`http:g` stays `http:g`), network-path, empty-path, absolute-path, and merge branches, with §5.2.3 path merge and a literal §5.2.4 two-buffer `remove_dot_segments` (all §5.4.1/§5.4.2 normal and abnormal examples resolve exactly).
- `uri_string.mbt` — §5.3 recomposition emitting delimiters precisely when components are present (even empty), so `Uri::parse(uri.to_string()) == uri` round-trips.
